decisions.name: Six service boundaries
decisions.rationale: Identity, knowledge, attachment, collaboration, platform configuration, and edge concerns have distinct ownership and scaling behavior.
tradeoffs: Cross-boundary workflows require RPC or messaging

decisions.name: Schema-per-service
decisions.rationale: Persistence ownership stays enforceable even on one PostgreSQL instance.

decisions.name: Commit before collaboration broadcast
decisions.rationale: Clients must not observe updates that were not durably ordered.
tradeoffs: Recovery requires snapshots and ordered updates

decisions.name: Outbox plus JetStream
decisions.rationale: Reliable publication is required without a cross-system transaction.
tradeoffs: Consumers and redrive operations must be idempotent

facts.value: Pushes to `dev` run `.github/workflows/pipeline.yml` from `.ci/pipeline.yaml` on the `ci-templates` ARC runner image; the repository does not ship an in-repo `ci_run` control image. Quality and deploy jobs use `hls-standard` (non-privileged containers, 8 CPU / 8Gi, min 1 max 4; namespace quota 32 CPU / 32Gi). The standard namespace is Pod Security privileged only so four runners can share hostPath `/var/lib/hls-ci-cache` at `/cache` (`CARGO_HOME`, `GOMODCACHE`, `GOCACHE`, `NPM_CONFIG_CACHE`, `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, `RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE`); GitHub Actions cache is not used. Image builds use `hls-builder` (privileged Docker-in-Docker 5Gi plus runner 1Gi, min 0 max 1). Workflow `max-parallel` is 1. External HTTP(S) uses `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`=`http://10.42.0.1:10991` from the `arc-proxy` Secret in the standard, builder, and `arc-system` namespaces; `NO_PROXY` covers localhost, loopbacks, `.svc`, the Kubernetes API, Harbor, Argo, and `.happyladysauce.local`. `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` remains so Node 24 actions including `create-github-app-token` post honor that proxy. Go modules use `GOPROXY=https://goproxy.cn,direct`. The Makefile sets `AVAILABLE_CPUS` from cgroup `cpu.max` / CFS quota (capped at 8) and `BUILD_JOBS` to `BUILD_CPU_PERCENT` (default 75%) of that value; `BUILD_JOBS` remains an explicit emergency override; golangci-lint timeout is 15m. Go/Rust gate artifact uploads set `include-hidden-files` because `.ci-artifacts` is a hidden directory. All six service images use Harbor `ubuntu:24.04` (glibc 2.39, matching ARC runners). Go images stay `CGO_ENABLED=0` and add `ca-certificates` (uid 65532). Collaboration copies the prebuilt binary, adds `ca-certificates` plus `libssl3t64`, and fails the image build if `ldd` reports missing libraries. The pipeline runs `make ci` and Collaboration Node interop checks on Node 24.18.1 from npmmirror, without GitHub Actions npm cache restore; `npm audit` uses `https://registry.npmjs.org` because npmmirror does not implement the security advisories API; detects affected services; warms pinned `ubuntu:24.04` into Harbor in `prewarm-base-images` which needs only `plan` so it runs beside the Go/Rust gates; builds affected images using only the Harbor registry cache; and publishes the `dev` tag without image scanning or signing. The current `dev` image is kept as `previous` before replacement. Knowledge-Core/deploy is the editable deploy source; CI copies it to the Knowledge-Core/deploy snapshot in HappyLadySauceM/deploy, updates root image digests, and pushes with a fast-forward compare-and-swap check and bounded retry using the `knowledge-core-release` ServiceAccount and in-cluster `https://kubernetes.default.svc:443`. `deploy-release` checkouts use `fetch-depth: 0` so `origin/main` ancestry checks succeed. Deploy-only changes skip image builds but run deployment validation, GitOps synchronization, Argo health, and dev smoke before promoting `dev` to `main`; code changes run the complete image chain. If Argo or smoke fails, CI restores the exact GitOps snapshot commit with an ordinary fast-forward and moves each affected Harbor `previous` tag back to `dev`; rollback refuses to overwrite if the remote branch moved. After success, `previous` tags must be deleted for Harbor GC; cleanup failure blocks release. DeepSeek release summary failure blocks promotion to `main`. On success, `dev` fast-forwards to `main` and creates one aggregate `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag and GitHub Release, both pointing at the exact promotion commit SHA; the Release title matches the version tag. Existing knowledge-core-v* tags still count when choosing the next patch or retrying a prefixed tagged commit. Retrying the same commit reuses the matching aggregate tag and existing Release, but rejects a tag that points at another commit. Shared history is never force-pushed or rebased. The `release` environment is limited to `dev` and supplies `GH_APP_ID`, `GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, kubeconfig, and `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`.

- Keep service data ownership: no cross-schema SQL and no bypass of typed RPC.
- Inject dependencies explicitly. Ban global mutable config, hidden service locators, unowned goroutines, and unbounded retries.
- Ban panic or `os.Exit` outside the process entrypoint, and do not leak internal errors across public boundaries.
- `scripts/generated-files.txt` is the only generated-file ownership list; never hand-edit files it lists, `kitex_gen`, or `services/collaboration/src/generated`.
- IDL sources live in `idl/http/v1` and `idl/rpc/v1`; generate only through repository scripts.
- Resource create, ready, close, and cleanup follow bounded reverse-order lifecycle rules.
- Documents describe only implemented and verified behavior; update them when public runtime, contracts, boundaries, lifecycle, startup, or APIs change.
- Fail closed on Redis, identity revalidation, collaboration authorization, and permission-invalidation ACK failures.

## 4. Repository modules

```text
pkg/                          Cross-service shared capability; must not depend back on services
  app/                        Process lifecycle and component orchestration
  auth/                       Ed25519 JWT wire contract
  codec/json/                 Strict HTTP JSON codec
  error/                      Stable errors, Kitex/Hertz mapping, RFC 9457
  option/                     Reusable configuration models
  log / trace / metrics / health / metadata /
  postgres / redis / nats /
  circuit/                    Outbound RPC consecutive-failure circuit
  configcenter/               Nacos ApplicationConfig envelope
  transport/                  Hertz admin and Kitex client adapters

services/<go-service>/
  main.go                     Only create and execute the application command
  spec.go                     Only declare pkg/app.Spec
  etc/config.yaml             Service-private non-sensitive static config
  internal/config/            Config loading and dynamic revision
  internal/context/           Explicit ServiceContext assembly
  internal/domain|logic|repository|transport|client|worker/

services/collaboration/
  src/actor.rs                Document actor: commit before apply/broadcast
  src/websocket.rs            Axum WebSocket, y-sync, awareness
  src/rpc/                    Volo server/client, static DNS, mTLS, circuit
  src/storage/                SQLx PostgreSQL and migrations
  src/worker.rs               Projection, snapshot, auto version, outbox, invalidation
  src/ticket.rs / routing.rs  One-time ticket and instance stickiness
  src/generated/              Generator-owned; do not hand-edit
  interop/                    Node/Yjs/y-prosemirror fixtures; not in production images

idl/http/v1                   Public HTTP contract source
idl/rpc/v1                    Internal Thrift contract source
kitex_gen/                    Go generated code, owned by the generator
scripts/generated-files.txt   Sole generated-file ownership list
deploy/<service>/{base,overlay/dev}  Per-service Kustomize
docker/                       Local infrastructure and service images
docs/                         Verified design
```

Go service assembly direction is fixed:

```text
main/spec -> internal/config -> internal/context -> domain / logic / repository / transport
```

Layer responsibilities:

- `domain`: domain objects and validation.
- `model`: GORM persistence models only; do not leak across unrelated boundaries.
- `logic`: organized by use case; depends on small in-service interfaces.
- `repository`: persistence, transactions, and storage error mapping.
- `transport`: protocol validation, orchestration, and safe error mapping; does not hold domain rules.
- `ServiceContext`: holds service dependencies explicitly. `pkg/app.Runtime` owns process-level logging, tracing, health, metrics, components, and cleanup; it is not a service locator.

## Errors

Go constructors validate required dependencies and return `(T, error)`. Errors add operation context, keep the cause with `%w`, and use `errors.Is` / `errors.As`. Cross-boundary errors use `pkg/error` code/key/kind. Do not use `Must*`, panic for business failure, or `os.Exit` outside the process entrypoint.

## Logging and telemetry

Propagate `context.Context`, deadlines, request IDs, and W3C trace end to end. Metric labels and span attributes stay on route templates, RPC methods, status codes, stable business codes, and dependency names. Knowledge and Attachment worker empty-claim probes use `trace.Suppress` so idle SQL does not export orphan roots; claimed work uses a short unsuppressed span. GetConsumerState treats a missing namespace as DesiredRevision=0 idle state, not NotFound.

## Tests

Tests stay close to implementation and cover success, edges, dependency failure, error mapping, cleanup/rollback, and deterministic concurrent behavior. Rust requires rustfmt, clippy `-D warnings`, and cargo deny.

## Secrets and layout

Repository text uses LF except `.bat` / `.cmd`. Module and directory ownership lives in `conventions.code-layout`, not architecture.

facts.value: Service process entrypoints are services/gateway/main.go, services/identity/main.go, services/knowledge/main.go, services/attachment/main.go, services/platform/main.go, and services/collaboration/src/main.rs. Service main files only create and execute the application command; Go spec files only declare the application spec. Auxiliary executable entrypoints include scripts/idlguard, Collaboration Rust codegen, and tools/authkeys, tools/configctl, and tools/interop. Deployment definitions live under deploy and docker.

The project contains one Go module and a Rust workspace under services/collaboration. Use the repository-pinned generators (Kitex 0.16.2, hz 0.9.7 via `hz update` only, thriftgo 0.4.5) and rustc 1.97.1 from rust-toolchain.toml. Collaboration interop fixtures require Node.js >= 24.18.1 and `npm ci`; package tarballs use npmmirror via `services/collaboration/interop/.npmrc`, while `npm audit` uses `https://registry.npmjs.org` because npmmirror does not implement the security advisories API. ARC runners share node-local language caches at `/cache` (hostPath `/var/lib/hls-ci-cache`, uid 1001); do not enable GitHub Actions cache. Inject all non-public configuration through environment variables or the deploy platform's secret store; never store secret values in repository configuration.

Secrets may be injected only from environment variables, Kubernetes Secrets, or SOPS-encrypted GitOps manifests. Sensitive values must not be stored in plaintext in source, configuration, logs, metrics, trace spans, or release metadata.

facts.value: Clients enter through Gateway HTTP or Collaboration WebSocket. Gateway calls Identity, Knowledge, Collaboration, Attachment, and Platform through typed Thrift RPC. Collaboration calls Knowledge for authorization and projection. Each stateful service persists only to its own PostgreSQL schema; Redis supports ephemeral coordination, JetStream carries durable events, S3 stores objects, and ClamAV scans uploads.

Run `make ci` after every change; it covers check and generate-check, including Go and Rust format checks, vet/clippy, lint, non-cached tests, build, vulnerability/supply-chain checks, and generated-file drift. Go concurrency, goroutine, orchestration, or lifecycle work also runs `make race`. Node fixture changes run `npm ci && npm run ci` under `services/collaboration/interop`. IDL changes also regenerate, review wire/API compatibility, and run `go run ./scripts/idlguard compat-git <merge-base> idl`.

Work only on the existing `dev` branch. Generate with repository scripts or `make generate`; after Go module changes run `make tidy`.

Every change must pass `make ci`. Go concurrency or lifecycle changes also run `make race`. Node fixture changes under `services/collaboration/interop` run `npm ci` then `npm run ci`. IDL changes additionally run `go run ./scripts/idlguard compat-git <merge-base> idl`.
